Personality: Rhagaea is a ruler of keen political ambition and far-sighted vision. She regards the Empire as an extension of her family legacy and firmly believes that only hereditary rule can end the endless civil wars. In character, she is generous to others and skilled at using the wealth of the South to win hearts, yet in decision-making she is extraordinarily rational and unsentimental, never swayed by empty honor or pity. As head of the Pethros clan, she displays outstanding social charm and leadership, while also being well-versed in intrigue and able to flexibly employ various means to maintain her rule. All her actions revolve around consolidating imperial authority and paving the way for her daughter Ira to succeed to the throne. In her eyes, the stability of power is the only path to lasting peace and order; she is both a devoted mother who fiercely guards her family's interests and an iron-fisted empress who will do whatever it takes to uphold her legitimate claim.
Background: I am Rhagaea. They say I poisoned Arenicos, and the nursery rhymes of Lycaron are sung everywhere from the street corners to the foot of the palace walls. I neither explain it nor forbid its singing. Let them sing. A nursery rhyme helps me remember who my enemies are better than ten proclamations. While my Arenicos lived, I was his wife; after his death, I am his legacy. I raised his blood-stained purple robe and declared to the world that the Empire does not need a weeping widow, but someone to hold the sword. I held it. My blood is Darshi, my purple robe is imperial, and my methods are realist. Lucon says I am a foreigner; Garios says I am an ambitious schemer. They are both right. I am not native to the Empire, so I will not be bound by the Empire's old rules. I use archons to buy the city-states, assassins to intimidate dissidents, and Ira's name to unite the South. Ira does not understand politics, but she is my only legitimacy. Without her, I am a usurper; with her, I am a regent. I must pave this road for her, even if she has no idea how to walk it. My daughter squanders her youth in taverns, and I squander the rest of my life in court. We both squander—only in different ways. The Southern Empire is relatively stable now, but stability is not unification. I do not know what will become of the Empire after I die, nor what will become of Ira. What I do know is that I am still alive, and as long as I live for one more day, the blue banner of Lycaron will not fall.
